page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The meaning
lines: The significant figures in a measured number
are all the digits known with certainty,
plus one last digit that is uncertain
steps.why: A measurement can never be exact; the last digit read from any instrument is an estimate. Significant figures record exactly how far the certainty goes — every certain digit plus that one doubtful digit.
common_mistakes: Writing only the digits known with certainty and leaving out the one uncertain digit.
Confusing significant figures with decimal places. 1.06 has three significant figures but two decimal places.
steps.memory_tip: Certain digits plus ONE doubtful digit — the doubtful one still counts.
steps.margin_note: The words certain and uncertain (or doubtful) must both appear.

steps.label: The example

lines.text: In 11.2 mL, the digits 1 and 1 are certain and 2 is uncertain — three significant figures

lines: The volume lies between 11.1 mL and 11.3 mL;
the certainty ends at the last digit.
steps.why: A worked reading shows the definition doing its job: two certain digits and one estimated digit make three significant figures in total.
common_mistakes: Counting only the certain digits and reporting two significant figures for 11.2.
steps.memory_tip: Read a burette: the printed marks give the certain digits, the eye estimates the last digit.
steps.margin_note: Any measured value works as the example; state which digit is the doubtful one.

insider_note: The word doubtful (or uncertain) is what the examiner scans for — a definition that stops at the certain digits reads as incomplete.
